story.headline: Dutch tour coach crash kills five in Graubünden
story.summary: A Dutch tour coach crashed in the Engadin, Graubünden, on Thursday afternoon, killing five and injuring about 40.
story.display_body: A Dutch tour coach crashed in the Engadin valley of canton Graubünden late Thursday afternoon (10 September), killing five people and injuring around 40. The coach — operated by Dutch tour operator OAD and carrying tourists from the Netherlands — hit a guardrail on the road between Susch and Zernez at about 4:45 p.m. local time, veered off, overturned and came to rest on its side; multiple helicopters were deployed in the rescue. Graubünden's cantonal police and public prosecutor say they are still clarifying the cause, which has not been established. Swiss President Guy Parmelin said he was "deeply shocked and dismayed" and offered condolences to the victims' families, promising a "comprehensive and thorough investigation."
story.why: it is one of the deadliest coach accidents on Swiss roads in years, and a cross-border tragedy that will draw scrutiny of alpine-road bus safety.

story.headline: Vaud PLR renews its three ministers
story.summary: Vaud's PLR endorsed sitting cabinet members Luisier, Moret and Borloz for the February–March 2027 cantonal executive election.
story.display_body: The PLR Vaud (the canton's liberal-radical party) endorsed its three sitting cantonal ministers — Christelle Luisier, Isabelle Moret and Frédéric Borloz — for re-election, at a party congress in Yvonand on Thursday 10 September. The trio, the party's only declared candidates, were confirmed by acclamation and will run for the Conseil d'État (Vaud's seven-member cantonal executive) at the February–March 2027 election as part of the centre-right "Alliance vaudoise," alongside Jean-François Thuillard of the UDC (Union démocratique du centre — the right-wing Swiss People's Party). The move locks in the incumbent centre-right slate roughly six months before the vote.

story.headline: France builds 2027 budget on 1% growth
story.summary: Lecornu's government presented a 2027 draft budget built on a 1% growth forecast that economists doubt will cut the deficit.
story.display_body: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's government unveiled the broad lines of France's 2027 draft budget on Friday 11 September, building it on a forecast of 1% growth (excluding inflation). Bercy (the French finance ministry) set out the assumptions, with final decisions on the text still to come; Le Monde reports that economists no longer believe the plan will actually reduce the deficit.
story.why: France's fiscal path is under close EU and market scrutiny after repeated deficit overruns, and a growth call many see as optimistic makes the promised consolidation harder to credit.

story.headline: Drone hits Chornobyl shelter, UN warns
story.summary: A drone struck the Chornobyl protective structure; UNDP chief De Croo warned it endangered millions, on a Ukraine visit Thursday.
story.display_body: A drone struck a protective structure at the decommissioned Chornobyl nuclear plant — an attack UN Development Programme (UNDP) chief Alexander De Croo called "gambling with the safety of millions of people," speaking from Kyiv on Thursday 10 September. De Croo (a former Belgian prime minister), on a visit focused on restoring Ukraine's energy grid, said the drone's origin must be established by investigation, though guards at the site — of the 1986 nuclear disaster — told him Russian drones overfly it daily. He said roughly half of Ukraine's energy infrastructure has already been damaged and that repair costs now exceed $600 billion (a World Bank/UN estimate) as a fifth winter of full-scale war approaches; UNDP has mobilised $1.3 billion in support.
story.why: strikes on or near nuclear sites and on the grid compound both nuclear-safety and humanitarian risks just as heating season begins.

story.headline: Hong Kong jails Tiananmen vigil leaders
story.summary: A Hong Kong court sentenced three Hong Kong Alliance leaders to five to seven-plus years for incitement to subversion.
story.display_body: A Hong Kong court on Friday 11 September sentenced three leaders of the disbanded Hong Kong Alliance to between five and seven-plus years in prison over the group's annual Tiananmen Square vigils. Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, received seven years; Chow Hang-tung, 41, seven years and three months; and Albert Ho, 74, five years and two months after pleading guilty — for "incitement to subversion" under Hong Kong's national security law. The three were convicted in August (covered here on 21 August); the Alliance, which organised the Victoria Park candlelight vigils now effectively banned, was fined HK$1.5 million (about US$191,000). Judges cited the group's call to "end one-party dictatorship." Foreign governments and rights groups criticised the ruling.

story.headline: Algeria severs ties with the UAE
story.summary: Algeria cut diplomatic relations with the UAE and moved to close its airspace, citing provocative and hostile acts.
story.display_body: Algeria severed diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates on Thursday 10 September, citing "provocative and hostile acts," and said it would begin closing its airspace to the UAE from Friday. Algiers gave the Emirati ambassador 48 hours and said it acted "after exhausting all avenues," though commercial flights to and from Algiers may continue until the end of 2026. Relations have been strained for years over what Algeria calls the UAE's expanding influence in North and West Africa; Algiers has accused Abu Dhabi of working to destabilise Libya, Mali and Sudan — including backing the Rapid Support Forces (RSF, a Sudanese paramilitary) in that country's civil war, a charge the UAE denies. The UAE said it hoped the decision would prove "temporary."

story.headline: Putin joins BRICS summit in New Delhi
story.summary: Putin arrived in New Delhi for the BRICS summit, with talks alongside Iran's Pezeshkian and India's Modi expected the same day.
story.display_body: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in New Delhi on Friday 11 September for a summit of the BRICS bloc (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa and newer members — the group of major emerging economies), with talks alongside Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian and India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi expected the same day. Le Temps reports the gathering convenes amid strains on the bloc's cohesion, from the conflict in the Middle East to the war in Ukraine.
